oracle_cases_note: 49 vendored oracle cases (40 ini_parse, 9 ini_get) + 27 audit-only extras (15 error line numbers, 12 get)
needs: buffer.Buffer (owned, dropped on every path incl. Err)
slices and sub-slices (&r [byte] returned from a function)
line splitting without a split function
text representation of a list (newline-terminated entries in one Buffer)
state in vars across a loop (current section, line number)
pitfalls: split at the FIRST '=' only (values may contain '=')
no trailing comments: ';' mid-line is part of the value
comments only at the start of the trimmed line
duplicate name: last value, first position
quote strip needs >= 2 bytes (a lone '"' is not a pair); only one pair; inside kept exactly
section name trimmed and may not contain [ ] =; text after ']' is malformed; lone '[' malformed
key must be ASCII only: non-ASCII key is malformed but non-ASCII value/section is fine
Err line number is 1-based and counts blank/comment lines and the first malformed line, not the last
final line without line feed still parsed; CR before LF ignored
buffer leaks / double drop on the Err path
ini_get must treat section '' as no prefix, and match the full name exactly (not as suffix)
difficulty_notes: The shapes are pinned in the plan: a list of settings is one Buffer of 'name=value\n' entries and Err carries the line number (the brief's List[Str] and message strings do not exist in cancho). The hard parts are ownership of Buffers across the raw/dedupe/parse chain and getting borrows right, not the INI grammar, which is fully specified in the plan. The vendored oracle only checks Err-ness; the audit adds line-number checks and a few extra get cases (single quote char, empty value, last-wins across re-opened sections).
